name: Resolve Merge Conflicts
problem: You try to pull or merge, but Git complains that there are conflicts. Someone else edited the exact same lines of code as you, and Git doesn't know which version to keep.

steps.title: Identify conflicting files
steps.description: Git stops the merge and marks the repository as 'merging'. Run status to see exactly which files need your attention.
steps.code:
git status
# Look for files under "Unmerged paths"

steps.title: Open files and fix conflicts manually
steps.description: Open the conflicting files in your editor. Git has injected conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`). Choose which code to keep (yours, theirs, or a combination of both), and delete the markers.
steps.code:
<<<<<<< HEAD (Current Change)
const dbHost = 'localhost';
=======
const dbHost = process.env.DB_HOST;
>>>>>>> feature-api (Incoming Change)

// Edit to become:
// const dbHost = process.env.DB_HOST;

steps.title: Stage the resolved files
steps.description: Once a file is fixed and saved, tell Git you've resolved it by staging it.

steps.title: Finalize the merge
steps.description: Once all conflicts are resolved and staged, commit to complete the merge process.
steps.code:
git commit
# Git will auto-populate the commit message with 'Merge...'

alternatives.title: Abort and bail out
alternatives.description: If the conflict is too complex and you want to give up and return to where you were before the merge started.
